title: GAME DESIGN HELP!!
author: Beginning-Sign1916
selftext:
Really need help around guys so this is my project after a month of working on it using claude. Features are good still working on fine tuning but graphics are really ugly and not what I wanted. Will appreciate if anyone here could point me to the right direction of getting proper good decent looking models and enviornment assets generation guide or prompts. This is a three.js game

https://preview.redd.it/ktipdl1qmgkh1.png?width=322&format=png&auto=webp&s=585bf219f128469ab8c544239b32aec737abacf6

comments.author: Street-Vermicelli800
comments.body: for the prompt ，define the art style once(low-poly/stylized,proportions,texture style,color palette,level of detail),and keep that same style across all the assets imo

replies.author: Beginning-Sign1916
replies.body:
I did prompt it that way but the thing is still it looks ugly. And what I am trying to achieve is this concept instead which is also a simple design. 

https://preview.redd.it/mhrs4jstzgkh1.png?width=286&format=png&auto=webp&s=2effeaf89869fa77aae65b51097211f0a9b9b30d

replies.author: yungastronot
replies.body:
You'll need real 3d models for this. You can check sketchfab or fab for free/paid ones you can use. You can try img to 3d AI like meshy but it'll be a lot less optimized that a hand modeled asset.

Theres nothing wrong with using threejs in fact this game in your similar style [https://messenger.abeto.co/](https://messenger.abeto.co/) illustrates whats possible with it. 

Yes the devs used webgl and threejs but they modeled the world and characters all by hand which is what you'll need to do to achieve this look.

replies.author: Beginning-Sign1916
replies.body: Yup that was also what I wanted to achieve cause of the style and design. I will try to find some similar on fab and also probably use meshy or even comfyui to generate out if possible. I try to keep my budget minimum. Thank you so much for your info and advice

comments.author: CommercialDoubt4628
comments.body: Maybe grab one model that’s close to the style you want and make that single asset look good in Three.js first?

replies.author: Beginning-Sign1916
replies.body: Yup agree with that I am still looking around on fab and other sites to see if I can find a good model commercial free

comments.author: ViralAtHelpshift
comments.body:
For the models, I'd try generating a few simple assets first and keep the style really consistent. With three.js, it can be tempting to generate everything separately and end up with models that all look like they're from different games.  
  
I'd also spend some time on lighting and materials before replacing everything. That alone can make pretty basic models look a lot better.

replies.author: Beginning-Sign1916
replies.body: Thank you for your advice I am still working on that and trying out. Hopefully I will be able to get it done by this week at least with a much better decent looking models
